The opposition never adequately explained how parental controls would work in practice.

words.ar: بما لا يدع مجالًا للشك المعقول
words.ex: We have shown beyond reasonable doubt that the harms are both real and widespread.
The decisive factor in this debate was the evidence on teenage mental health.

dialogue.t: Ladies and gentlemen, this debate has come down to three key clashes: mental health, personal freedom, and who should bear responsibility.
Surely the opposition won the freedom clash? We showed that teenagers value their independence online.
Where the opposition fell short was in explaining why that freedom matters when the platforms themselves are designed to be addictive. Freedom to scroll compulsively is hardly freedom at all.
But we offered a solution — better digital education in schools.
You did, yet you never adequately responded to our evidence that even well-informed teenagers struggle to resist algorithmic design.
That's a fair criticism, I suppose. We assumed knowledge would be enough.
Ultimately, we have shown beyond reasonable doubt that, on the issues that matter most, social media does more harm than good to teenagers. We are proud to propose.

grammar.title: Present perfect vs past simple in summary speeches
grammar.ar: في خطاب الختام نستخدم المضارع التام (we have shown) لعرض نتيجة النقاش كإنجاز له أثر مستمر حتى الآن، ونستخدم الماضي البسيط (they claimed, they never responded) للإشارة إلى ما حدث في لحظة محددة من المناظرة. يميل المتعلمون العرب إلى استخدام الماضي البسيط في كل الحالات لأن العربية لا تفرّق بينهما بالطريقة نفسها، لكن هذا التمييز يمنح الخطاب قوة ودقة.
examples: Throughout this debate, we have demonstrated that the risks are systemic, not isolated.
In their first speech, the opposition claimed that regulation would be ineffective.
They have still not explained why the evidence from other countries should be ignored.

words.ex: She opened with such an arresting image that the entire hall fell silent within seconds.
A speaker has roughly fifteen seconds to captivate an audience before attention begins to drift.

words.ar: منظومة ريادة الأعمال (البيئة الداعمة للمشاريع الناشئة)
words.ex: The Kingdom's entrepreneurial ecosystem has matured remarkably, with incubators now springing up in cities well beyond Riyadh.
Rather than reciting figures, he began with a vivid anecdote about his cousin's first market stall.
Your opening line sets the tone for everything that follows, so choose it with care.
Young founders in Jeddah have repeatedly defied expectations by scaling their ventures internationally.

dialogue.t: So, Faisal, you've got two minutes in front of the whole school. How do you intend to open?
I was going to start with 'Good morning, today I'll talk about entrepreneurship.'
Safe, but forgettable. Half the assembly will have tuned out before you reach your second sentence. Try something that jolts them.
All right, how about this: 'What if I told you that the person who will found the Kingdom's next great company might be sitting in this very hall?'
Much better. That makes it personal at once. Could you add a sense of how quickly things have changed?
'Just a decade ago, few would have imagined that a Saudi teenager could launch an app from her bedroom and sell it across the Gulf.'
Excellent. And if you want to finish the hook with weight, you might say: 'It is no exaggeration to say that our generation is rewriting what it means to work.'
Or I could paint a scene first: 'Picture, if you will, a small café in Al-Khobar where three students are sketching a business plan on a napkin.' Then I'd hit them with the question.

grammar.title: Rhetorical Openers: Hypotheticals, Imperatives and Emphatic Framing
grammar.ar: تعتمد الافتتاحيات الخطابية القوية على تراكيب تُشرك المستمع مباشرة، مثل الأمر المهذّب (Picture, if you will…) الذي يدعو الجمهور إلى التخيّل، والسؤال الافتراضي (What if I told you that…?) الذي يثير الفضول. أما (It is no exaggeration to say that…) فهي صيغة تأكيدية تستخدم فاعلاً شكلياً (It) لإبراز الفكرة الرئيسة. وتُستخدم (few would have imagined) بصيغة الماضي الشرطي التام للتعبير عن أمر لم يكن متوقعاً في الماضي لكنه تحقق اليوم.
examples: Picture, if you will, a classroom where every student leaves with a viable business idea.
What if I told you that most successful founders failed at least once before they succeeded?
Just a decade ago, few would have imagined that young Saudis would be pitching to international investors.

words.ex: The speech built to a tricolon so crisp that students were quoting it in the corridor afterwards.
Without parallel structure, even a strong idea can sound clumsy and lopsided.
Listen to the cadence of great speeches: the rhythm often matters as much as the content.
Her closing lines galvanised the student body into registering for the election in record numbers.
'Listen, include, deliver' became the rallying cry of his entire campaign.
Promises about longer library hours resonated with students far more than vague talk of change.

dialogue.t: Reem, I've read your campaign speech. The ideas are solid, but it doesn't quite sing yet.
I know. It sounds like a list of complaints rather than a vision. How do I give it rhythm?
Group your promises in threes and keep the grammar identical. Try your central line again.
'We need a council that listens, we deserve a council that acts, and we are ready for a council that delivers.'
Now that has cadence. What about your point on student clubs?
'Not only will I expand the clubs, but I will also make sure every student has a voice in how they're run.'
Good. And to answer people who say you're too young or inexperienced?
'It is not the length of your record that matters, but the strength of your commitment. And the more we participate, the more we shape the school we want.'

grammar.title: Parallelism, Correlatives and the Comparative Correlative
grammar.ar: التوازي يعني استخدام البنية النحوية نفسها في عدة عبارات متتالية، مما يمنح الكلام إيقاعاً يسهل تذكّره. وفي (Not only… but also…) يجب أن يتماثل ما بعد الجزأين نحوياً، وإذا بدأت الجملة بـ Not only وجب قلب الفعل المساعد (Not only will I…). أما (The more…, the more…) فهي مقارنة مزدوجة تعبّر عن تلازم التغيّر بين أمرين، ويأتي بعد كل جزء فاعل وفعل.
examples: We need fairness, we deserve respect, and we are ready for responsibility.
It is not the size of the budget that matters, but the wisdom with which it is spent.
The more we listen to one another, the more we discover how much we share.

words.ex: Sharing her own experience as a peer mentor lent her argument immediate credibility.

words.ar: يشهد على، يؤكد بناءً على خبرة
words.ex: Any teacher can attest to the toll that exam pressure takes on students in the final term.
The survey results point unequivocally to a need for accessible counselling services.
Breaking the stigma around mental health is often harder than funding the services themselves.
We are asking the council to allocate funding for a pilot programme in three schools.
By weaving data with personal testimony, the team made a compelling case to the panel.

dialogue.t: Remember, the panel will be community leaders. They'll want to know why they should trust you before they trust your proposal.
That's why I'm opening with ethos: 'As someone who has volunteered on our school's peer-support line for two years, I can attest that many students suffer in silence.'
Strong. Then you need to move them. Where does pathos come in?
'Consider, for a moment, how it would feel to be sixteen, overwhelmed, and convinced that asking for help would bring shame on your family.'
That will land, especially given the stigma we're up against. But don't let emotion carry the whole argument.
No, logos comes next: 'The figures speak for themselves: in our own survey of four hundred students, more than half reported persistent anxiety.'
And your conclusion from that data?
'The evidence points unequivocally to one thing: early, accessible support is not a luxury but a necessity, and that is why we are asking you to fund it.'

grammar.title: Language of Authority: Boosters and Evidential Phrasing
grammar.ar: لإقناع جمهور رسمي نستخدم عبارات تعزّز اليقين (boosters) مثل unequivocally وclearly وundeniably لإظهار الثقة بالأدلة. وتُستخدم (As someone who has + التصريف الثالث) لبناء المصداقية عبر الخبرة الشخصية، إذ يربط المضارع التام التجربة الماضية بسلطة المتحدث الحالية. أما (Consider, for a moment, how it would feel to…) فتجمع بين الأمر المهذّب والشرط الافتراضي (would) لدعوة الجمهور إلى التعاطف.
examples: As someone who has organised three awareness campaigns, I can attest that students are eager for support.
Consider, for a moment, how it would feel to have nobody to turn to.
The figures speak for themselves: referrals have doubled in just two years.

words.ex: My grandfather was a voracious reader who devoured history books in both Arabic and English.
Schools have a responsibility to foster a genuine love of reading, not merely to test comprehension.
Attendance at the school library dwindled as phones became students' main source of entertainment.
A single great novel can rekindle a teenager's interest in books.
Reading widely nurtures the intellectual curiosity that no curriculum can fully provide.
Pause before your key line so that it lands with impact.

dialogue.t: Your speech on reading culture is well researched, Nora, but the key points are buried in flat sentences.
So how do I make them stand out without simply shouting?
Use word order. Instead of 'We have never had so many books available', try inverting it.
'Never before has knowledge been so accessible, and yet never before have we read so little.'
Much more striking. Now your solution: how do we turn things around?
'Only by making reading a shared habit, at home and at school, can we rekindle a culture that is dwindling.'
And the personal story about your grandfather's library?

'Not until I opened his old notebooks did I realise how much reading had shaped him. It was his curiosity, not his degree, that ultimately defined him. What truly matters, then, is not how many books we own, but how many we open.'

grammar.title: Negative Inversion and Cleft Sentences for Emphasis
grammar.ar: القلب بعد العبارات السلبية أو المقيِّدة (Never before, Only by, Not until) يعني تقديم الفعل المساعد على الفاعل كما في السؤال، مثل: Never before has… وهو أسلوب رسمي يمنح الجملة قوة درامية. أما الجمل المشطورة (cleft sentences) فتُبرز عنصراً بعينه، إما بصيغة (It was … that …) أو بصيغة (What … is …). ولاحظ أنه مع Not until يقع القلب في الجملة الرئيسة لا في جملة until نفسها.
examples: Never before has a generation had access to so many stories.
Not until we lost our local bookshop did we realise what it meant to the neighbourhood.
What truly matters is not speed of reading but depth of understanding.

words.ex: Opening heritage sites to mass tourism remains a contentious issue among historians.
Tourism is a central pillar of the Kingdom's strategy for economic diversification.
AlUla's heritage sites draw visitors who might never have considered Saudi Arabia a decade ago.
Sustainable tourism means growth that protects the very landscapes visitors come to see.
To put the numbers into perspective, the target is roughly equal to the population of several major cities combined.
In her final minute, she drew the threads together into a single, coherent message.

dialogue.t: Your talk on Saudi tourism has four parts, Omar. That's a lot for listeners to hold in their heads.
I know. In rehearsal, people lost track somewhere around the environmental section.
Then signpost every transition. How do you move from the economic case to the next part?
'Having established why tourism matters for economic diversification, I now turn to the question of who actually benefits.'
Clear. And the section on heritage sites, which you know will divide opinion?
'This brings me to my second, and perhaps more contentious, point: can we welcome millions of visitors without endangering places like AlUla?'
Good. Your visitor targets sound abstract, though. Make them concrete.
'To put this into perspective, imagine the population of an entire city arriving each year. Let me draw these threads together: growth, fairness and preservation must advance hand in hand.'

grammar.title: Perfect Participle Clauses and Discourse Markers
grammar.ar: تُستخدم الجملة المصدّرة بـ (Having + التصريف الثالث) للإشارة إلى أن فعلاً قد اكتمل قبل الفعل الرئيس، وهي أداة مثالية للانتقال بين أجزاء الخطاب لأنها تلخّص ما سبق وتمهّد لما يلي. ويجب أن يكون فاعل جملة المشاركة هو نفسه فاعل الجملة الرئيسة (Having established…, I…). أما عبارات مثل (This brings me to…) و(Let me draw these threads together) فهي علامات خطابية ترشد المستمع إلى بنية الحجة.
examples: Having examined the economic benefits, I now turn to the social impact.
This brings me to my final, and arguably most urgent, point: sustainability.
Having heard the objections, we can now weigh them against the evidence.

words.ex: A speech without a clear call to action may inspire, but it rarely changes behaviour.
The student union mobilised over two hundred volunteers for the Ramadan food drive.
Volunteering cultivates a sense of civic responsibility that lasts well beyond school.
Genuine altruism asks for nothing in return, not even recognition.
Even an hour a week can make a tangible difference to an elderly neighbour.
It is the final thirty seconds of a speech that usually leave a lasting impression.

dialogue.t: Lama, your speech on volunteering is moving, but it ends with 'Thank you for listening.' That wastes your strongest moment.
You're right. I want people to walk out and actually sign up. How should I close?
Distil your message into one sentence they can't forget.
'If you take nothing else from today, let it be this: an hour of your time can change someone's entire week.'
Lovely. Now shift the debate away from whether they'll help.
'The question is no longer whether we can make a tangible difference, but how quickly we choose to begin.'
And finish by appealing to their values, not just their sense of duty.
'Let us volunteer — not because it looks good on an application, but because our community deserves the best of us. The choice, ultimately, is ours.'

grammar.title: Hortatory 'Let us' and Contrastive Reframing
grammar.ar: تُستخدم (Let us + المصدر) للحثّ الجماعي، فهي تُشرك المتحدث مع الجمهور وتمنح الخاتمة طابعاً رسمياً ملهماً، أكثر وقاراً من الصيغة المختصرة Let's. ويُعدّ التركيب (not because…, but because…) أسلوباً تقابلياً يرفض دافعاً سطحياً ليقدّم دافعاً أعمق. أما (The question is no longer whether…, but how…) فتعيد صياغة النقاش، فتعدّ المبدأ أمراً محسوماً وتنقل التركيز إلى التنفيذ.
examples: Let us act — not because we are told to, but because we believe it is right.
The question is no longer whether young people care, but how we harness that care.
If you take nothing else from today, let it be this: small acts accumulate into lasting change.

words.ex: Submitting an essay written entirely by a chatbot is a clear breach of academic integrity.

words.ar: إسناد (التفكير) إلى جهة أخرى / الاتكال على غيرك في التفكير
words.ex: If students outsource their thinking to AI, they may never learn to construct an argument themselves.
Generative AI is a double-edged sword: it can spark creativity or stifle it entirely.
Without clear accountability, nobody knows who is to blame when an AI tool gives false information.
Some students have found ingenious ways to circumvent plagiarism-detection software.
An outright ban on AI might stifle the very innovation schools claim to encourage.

dialogue.t: So, should students be allowed to use AI tools for their schoolwork? I'm genuinely torn on this one.
I'd say it is arguably a question of how we use them rather than whether we use them at all. Banning them outright seems rather naive.
Perhaps, but there is a fine line between using AI as a study aid and letting it do the work for you. Where does brainstorming end and cheating begin?
That's fair. One could make a compelling case that AI levels the playing field for weaker writers, though it could equally make them dependent on it.
Exactly. And teachers can't always tell the difference, which undermines the whole assessment system.
To my mind, the real issue is not whether students will use AI, but who takes responsibility when it's misused: the student, the school, or the companies building these tools.
So you'd favour clear guidelines over prohibition?
Absolutely. Transparent rules, plus assessments that reward original reasoning rather than polished prose.

grammar.title: Hedging and contrastive focus
grammar.ar: في النقاش الرسمي نستخدم كلمات مثل arguably و one could make a case لتخفيف حدّة الرأي وإظهار الموضوعية بدلاً من الجزم المطلق. ويُستخدم التركيب The real issue is not whether ... but who/what ... لإعادة توجيه النقاش نحو النقطة الأهم، فننفي الفكرة الشائعة أولاً ثم نُبرز الفكرة التي نراها جوهرية. هذا الأسلوب يجعل حجتك تبدو أكثر نضجاً وإقناعاً أمام المستمعين.
examples: It is arguably a matter of education rather than regulation.
One could make a compelling case that AI enhances learning, though the risks are considerable.
The real issue is not whether the technology works, but who controls it.

words.ex: Planting ten billion trees is a laudable goal, but it requires enormous water resources.
Engineers are still assessing the feasibility of building a city without cars.
The success of the project hinges on attracting foreign investment and skilled workers.
Combating desertification is one of the central aims of the Saudi Green Initiative.
We should temper our optimism with a realistic look at the costs involved.
NEOM has become the flagship project of Vision 2030, attracting global attention.

dialogue.t: What's your take on mega-projects like NEOM and the Saudi Green Initiative? Are they realistic?
While the ambition behind them is undeniably laudable, it remains to be seen whether they can deliver on such bold promises.
I agree the scale is staggering. But surely the extent to which they succeed hinges on long-term commitment rather than initial funding?
Precisely, and on sustainable water management too. Planting billions of trees in an arid climate is no small feat.
Still, were NEOM to succeed, it would redefine what urban living looks like, not just in the region but globally.
Undoubtedly. It could become a model for carbon-neutral cities. I just think we should temper our enthusiasm with some hard questions.
Such as?
Such as cost, environmental impact during construction, and whether people will actually want to live there. It would be premature to conclude that it's either a triumph or a failure at this stage.

grammar.title: Inverted conditionals with 'Were ... to'
grammar.ar: في اللغة الرسمية يمكننا حذف if وقلب ترتيب الجملة الشرطية باستخدام Were + الفاعل + to + الفعل، وذلك للحديث عن احتمالات افتراضية في المستقبل. فبدلاً من If NEOM succeeded نقول Were NEOM to succeed. هذا الأسلوب شائع في الخطابات والمناظرات ويضفي طابعاً رسمياً وبلاغياً على الكلام.
examples: Were the initiative to succeed, it would transform the region's environment.
Were investors to withdraw, the project would face serious delays.
Were we to ignore these warnings, we would be making a costly mistake.

words.ex: It is reductive to describe tradition as simply resistance to change.
Museums and oral history projects help safeguard our cultural memory.
Some elders worry about the gradual erosion of Arabic among young people who mostly speak English online.
Intergenerational conversations at family gatherings keep traditions alive.
Many young Saudis manage to reconcile global ambitions with deep-rooted values.
A sense of rootedness can give young people the confidence to explore the world.

dialogue.t: Do you think young Saudis are losing touch with their heritage as the country opens up to the world?
Not necessarily. Far from being at odds, tradition and modernity can actually reinforce each other. Look at how Diriyah has been restored as a cultural destination.
That's a good example. And it would be reductive to suggest that studying abroad or working for global companies automatically weakens one's identity.
Absolutely. If anything, living abroad often makes people more aware of who they are.
Even so, much as I value these new opportunities, I cannot help but feel that some things are quietly slipping away, like dialects and family storytelling.
I see what you mean. Many teenagers communicate more in English online than in Arabic.
Exactly. What we risk losing, if we are not careful, is the intergenerational bond that passes values down naturally.
Then perhaps the solution lies in making heritage relevant, through digital archives, creative projects, and simply spending more time with our grandparents.

grammar.title: Concession with 'Much as' and 'Far from'
grammar.ar: يُستخدم التركيب Much as + جملة بمعنى «مع أنني... كثيراً» للاعتراف بفكرة ما قبل تقديم رأي مخالف أو تحفّظ، وهو أقوى وأكثر رسمية من although. أما Far from + اسم أو فعل بصيغة ing فيعني «بعيداً عن / على العكس تماماً من»، ويُستخدم لنفي فكرة شائعة بقوة ثم تقديم الحقيقة المعاكسة.
examples: Much as I admire globalisation, I worry about its impact on local languages.
Far from weakening our identity, travel can deepen our appreciation of home.
Much as we embrace change, certain values must remain non-negotiable.

words.ex: Disinformation campaigns often target elections and public health.
Algorithms tend to amplify sensational content because it generates more clicks.
The onus is on platforms to remove harmful content quickly.
Critics fear that strict regulation could slide into censorship.
Media literacy should be taught in schools so students can spot fake news.

words.ar: غرفة الصدى (بيئة لا يسمع فيها المرء إلا آراء تشبه آراءه)
words.ex: Social media can trap users in an echo chamber where their beliefs are never challenged.

dialogue.t: Who should be responsible for stopping fake news: platforms, governments, or the users themselves?
Personally, I think the onus should surely be on the platforms to fix their algorithms. They profit from viral content, after all.
Granted, platforms have enormous influence; nevertheless, they can't fact-check billions of posts in real time.
True. So should governments step in with stricter laws?
Possibly, but where exactly do we draw the line between protecting the public and restricting legitimate debate?
That's the dilemma. Heavy-handed regulation could easily be seen as censorship.
Which is why I'd argue individual users matter most. Unless people learn to verify sources before sharing, we will continue to see rumours spread faster than facts.
So maybe it's a shared responsibility: smarter algorithms, sensible regulation, and media literacy taught from an early age.

grammar.title: Conceding and countering: 'Granted, ...; nevertheless, ...'
grammar.ar: في المناظرات يُعدّ الاعتراف بحجة الطرف الآخر قبل الردّ عليها أسلوباً مقنعاً جداً. نبدأ بـ Granted (أي «صحيح / مُسلَّم به») لقبول جزء من رأي المحاور، ثم نستخدم nevertheless أو even so لتقديم الحجة المضادة. لاحظ استخدام الفاصلة المنقوطة (;) قبل nevertheless في الكتابة الرسمية.
examples: Granted, regulation has its risks; nevertheless, doing nothing is far more dangerous.
Granted, users should think before sharing; nevertheless, platforms design the systems that reward outrage.
Unless we invest in media literacy, we will continue to see misinformation thrive.

words.ex: Automation has already transformed manufacturing and logistics.
Some routine administrative jobs may become obsolete within a decade.
Companies are investing heavily in upskilling their employees to work alongside AI.
Employers increasingly value adaptability over narrow technical knowledge.
In a rapidly changing economy, lifelong learning is no longer optional.
Governments must plan for job displacement caused by new technologies.

dialogue.t: How do you think automation will change the careers available to our generation?
Dramatically. Should AI-driven systems become the norm in sectors like finance and healthcare, many entry-level roles will simply disappear.
That sounds rather bleak. But new jobs will emerge too, won't they?
In all likelihood, they will, albeit in fields we can barely imagine today. Twenty years ago, nobody was a data scientist or a content creator.
So what should schools be focusing on?
Insofar as machines handle routine tasks, it makes sense to prioritise creativity, critical thinking and emotional intelligence.
I agree. It is not so much what you know as how quickly you can learn something new.
Exactly. Adaptability will be the real currency of the future job market.

grammar.title: Inverted 'Should' conditionals and 'albeit'
grammar.ar: يمكن استبدال If ... should بقلب الجملة لتبدأ بـ Should + الفاعل + الفعل، للتعبير عن احتمال مستقبلي بأسلوب رسمي، مثل: Should automation become the norm. أما albeit فتعني «وإن كان / ولو أنّ» وتُتبَع عادةً بصفة أو ظرف أو عبارة قصيرة لا بجملة كاملة، وتُستخدم لإضافة تحفّظ بإيجاز.
examples: Should robots replace factory workers, retraining programmes will be essential.
In all likelihood, AI will create new jobs, albeit not at the same pace it eliminates old ones.
It is not so much the technology as our response to it that will shape the future.

words.ex: The COVID-19 crisis exposed serious gaps in pandemic preparedness worldwide.
KSrelief has coordinated relief efforts in dozens of countries.
Charities were able to mobilise volunteers within hours of the earthquake.
Health crises disproportionately affect the poorest communities.
The equitable distribution of vaccines proved far harder than developing them.

words.ar: بالنظر إلى ما حدث لاحقاً / بعد فوات الأوان وبوضوح الرؤية
words.ex: With the benefit of hindsight, earlier travel restrictions might have slowed the spread.

dialogue.t: Looking back at the COVID-19 pandemic, what lessons do you think the world should have learned?
With the benefit of hindsight, it's clear that most countries were woefully underprepared. Had governments been more proactive, thousands of lives might well have been saved.
And the global response was, to put it mildly, uneven. Wealthy nations secured vaccines while poorer countries waited months.
Exactly. I would go so far as to say that vaccine inequality was one of the greatest moral failures of the crisis.
That's a strong claim, but I think it's justified. On a more positive note, humanitarian organisations did step up.
Certainly. Saudi Arabia, through KSrelief, provided medical supplies and funding to many countries, and pledged significant support to the WHO.
And charity is deeply rooted in our culture, through zakat and sadaqah. That spirit was very visible during the pandemic.
True. The challenge now is turning that generosity into long-term systems, so we're not caught off guard next time.

grammar.title: Inverted third conditional with 'Had'
grammar.ar: للحديث عن ماضٍ افتراضي لم يحدث، يمكننا حذف if وتقديم had على الفاعل: Had + الفاعل + التصريف الثالث، ثم might/would have + التصريف الثالث. مثلاً: Had they acted sooner بدلاً من If they had acted sooner. يُستخدم هذا الأسلوب كثيراً عند تحليل الأحداث الماضية واستخلاص الدروس منها بأسلوب رسمي.
examples: Had the warnings been taken seriously, the outbreak might well have been contained.
Had more funding been available, aid agencies could have reached remote villages.
I would go so far as to say that international cooperation saved millions of lives.

words.ex: My long-term aspiration is to work in international law, ideally on human rights cases.
What I find most rewarding about philosophy is that every lesson is intellectually stimulating.

dialogue.t: Let's begin. Could you tell me what you enjoy most about your current studies?
Certainly. What I find most rewarding about studying history is the way it forces you to question narratives you once took for granted.
And how would you describe yourself as a learner?
I'd like to think that I'm quite disciplined, although I do have a tendency to leave essays until the last minute when a topic doesn't grip me.
Is there anything you find particularly challenging?
If I'm honest, public speaking used to terrify me. Joining the debate club was a deliberate attempt to confront that fear, and it's paid off.
And what about the future? Where do you see yourself in ten years?
Looking ahead, I envisage myself working for an international organisation, perhaps in diplomacy, where I could put my languages to good use.

grammar.title: Cleft sentences for emphasis (What I find... is...)

What I'd like to achieve, above all, is a career that feels genuinely meaningful.

dialogue.t: Shall we start by considering which of these pictures shows the most pressing urban problem?
Good idea. To my mind, it's the traffic congestion. It affects almost everyone, every single day.
I take your point, but wouldn't you agree that the lack of affordable housing has more serious long-term consequences?
That's fair. Rising rents can force families out of the city entirely, which is arguably more damaging than a slow commute.
Exactly. And it's closely tied to gentrification, which we can see in the third photo.
So, if I've understood you correctly, you're suggesting that housing is the root cause, and that many other problems stem from it?
Precisely. Congestion is partly a result of people being priced out and having to commute in from the suburbs.
That's a persuasive argument. Shall we settle on affordable housing as the priority, then?

words.ex: Talent alone is rarely enough; sustained success requires drive and resilience.

The relentless pursuit of top grades can lead to burnout among teenagers.
For many people, personal fulfilment matters far more than wealth or status.
Rapid career success often comes at a price, notably in terms of family life.
Salary is a rather crude yardstick for measuring success.

dialogue.t: Here is your card: 'Is ambition always a positive quality?' You should talk about personal goals, society's expectations, and the cost of success. Please begin.
The question raises the issue of whether ambition is inherently good, or whether its value depends on what drives it and what it costs us.
On a personal level, ambition can be enormously motivating. It gives us direction and pushes us beyond what we believed we were capable of.
Turning to the second aspect, society often imposes a very narrow definition of success, usually measured in salary or status, and young people can feel immense pressure to conform to it.
A case in point would be students who choose medicine purely to satisfy family expectations, only to discover that they have no passion for it.
As for the cost, unchecked ambition can lead to burnout, damaged relationships and a sense of emptiness even after goals are reached.
All things considered, I'd conclude that ambition is a positive force only when it is self-directed and balanced by an awareness of what truly brings us fulfilment.
Thank you. That was very well organised.

grammar.title: Nominalisation for formal, cohesive speech
grammar.ar: التسمية (Nominalisation) تعني تحويل الأفعال أو الصفات إلى أسماء، مثل ambitious إلى ambition و succeed إلى success. هذا الأسلوب يجعل الحديث الطويل أكثر رسمية وتماسكًا، ويساعدك على الربط بين الأفكار بسلاسة عندما تتحدث لمدة دقيقتين. وهو سمة أساسية في لغة المستوى C2 الأكاديمية.

words.ex: Just to play devil's advocate, couldn't technology actually bring people closer together?

I agree to some extent, but I think the argument is slightly oversimplified.

dialogue.t: Do you think it's possible for a society to be both completely free and completely fair?
That's a thought-provoking question; I suppose it comes down to how we define 'fair' in the first place.
And would you say technology makes us more or less free?
It depends to a large extent on who controls that technology. In the hands of individuals it can be liberating, but in the hands of a few corporations, far less so.
So is surveillance ever justified?
I'd be inclined to say it can be, in cases of genuine public safety, although the risk of abuse is considerable.
But who decides what counts as 'genuine public safety'?
On reflection, I might revise that slightly: surveillance is only defensible when there is independent oversight and full transparency about how data is used.

grammar.title: Hedging with tentative language
grammar.ar: التحوّط (Hedging) هو استخدام لغة غير قاطعة للتعبير عن رأي بحذر، مثل I'd be inclined to say و It could be argued و I suppose و might. هذا يُظهر نضجًا فكريًّا ويمنحك وقتًا للتفكير، كما يسمح لك بتعديل رأيك لاحقًا دون أن تبدو متناقضًا. المتحدث في مستوى C2 نادرًا ما يقدّم آراءه المعقّدة بصيغة مطلقة.
examples: I'd be inclined to say that education matters more than legislation in this case.
It could be argued that social media has, if anything, made us lonelier.
There might well be exceptions, but on the whole I think the principle holds.

dialogue.t: Honourable delegates, I'd like to draw your attention to the first chart on youth employment across the region.
As this graph clearly illustrates, unemployment among 18- to 24-year-olds rose steadily between 2015 and 2021, before plateauing at around 28 percent.
What is particularly striking here is the disparity between young men and young women, with female unemployment almost ten points higher.
Could you explain what might account for that gap?
Certainly. When we compare this with the second chart on vocational training, we see far lower female enrolment. This suggests, albeit tentatively, that access to training may be a key factor.
So would you recommend expanding training programmes for women?
That would be a logical step. However, these findings should be treated with caution, given that the survey covered only urban areas and the sample size was relatively small.
Further research, particularly in rural communities, is therefore essential before any firm policy conclusions are drawn.

grammar.title: Concessive structures: albeit, although, while
grammar.ar: تُستخدم أدوات التنازل مثل albeit و although و while لتقديم استنتاج مع الاعتراف بحدوده في الوقت نفسه، وهذا أساسي عند عرض البيانات بموضوعية. كلمة albeit رسمية جدًّا وتعني (وإن كان)، وتأتي عادةً قبل صفة أو ظرف أو عبارة قصيرة، لا قبل جملة كاملة. أما although و while فتأتي بعدهما جملة كاملة.
examples: The data points to a recovery, albeit a slow and uneven one.

While the correlation is strong, it does not in itself prove causation.

dialogue.t: Your presentation focused on youth unemployment, but isn't the real problem that schools simply aren't preparing students for modern jobs?
That's an excellent question — let me unpack it. There are really two issues here: the curriculum itself, and the speed at which the job market is changing.
But surely the government should be held responsible for that?
If I may rephrase your question: you're asking whether policymakers have failed to adapt education to economic reality, is that right?
Exactly. And what will happen to unemployment in the next decade?
I'm not in a position to make precise forecasts, but what I can say is that every reliable study points to digital skills becoming increasingly decisive.
To return to your original point, yes, I'd concede that schools bear part of the responsibility, though employers and governments must share it.
Thank you, that's a very balanced answer.

grammar.title: Formal politeness: If I may... / I'm not in a position to...
